title: Onramp kit & latency-backed BOM heuristics (first-wave)
body:
Purpose:
This quick-pass worksheet is intended for early procurement and runbook planning when onboarding a customer for a Private/VPC deployment. It focuses on a small first-wave fleet (1–8 racks) where latency SLAs drive SKU choices and spare capacity planning rather than pure cheapest TCO. This is not the final procurement sheet — it is a heuristics-driven starter that teams (sales-eng, solutions, infra) can iterate on during scoping calls.

Key assumptions (first-wave):
- Target customers: mid-market to enterprise, realtime chat/generation workloads.
- Latency SLA target: p95 <= 200 ms for 1–2k concurrent short-chat sessions (avg 80 tokens/session).
- Warm KV cache hit expected: 35% for reuse-friendly apps.
- Burst profile: 3x baseline sustained for short windows (5–10m).
- Procurement lead time: 6–12 weeks for GPUs; 2–4 weeks for chassis + networking.

Quick heuristic steps (how to use):
1) Capture expected TPS (requests/sec) and tokens/session (T). Baseline R = expected concurrent sessions / average session length seconds. Example below uses sessions concurrently rather than TPS.
2) Choose latency anchoring model: choose low-latency variant (e.g., 1.5B quantized vs 7B) to meet p95 SLA.
3) Estimate per-GPU steady throughput for chosen model (tokens/sec or requests/sec) from internal bench table. Use conservative 70% of bench for first-wave.
4) Compute needed GPUs = ceil( (baseline_tokens_per_sec * 1.0) / (per_gpu_tokens_sec * utilization_target) ).
5) Add spare buffer: +20% for first-wave (higher if customer needs 99.9% SLA or global redundancy).
6) Translate GPUs to racks using target rack density (GPUs per chassis * chassis per rack).

Representative sample calculation (scenario A - low-latency chat):
- Customer: 1.5k concurrent short sessions, avg 80 tokens/session, average think time 12s between messages. Baseline tokens/sec = (1500 * 80) / 12 = 10,000 tokens/sec.
- Model choice: 7B-opt-llama variant quantized (bench per-GPU ~9k tokens/sec on A100-80GB equivalent). Conservative first-wave throughput = 9k * 0.7 = 6.3k tokens/sec per GPU.
- Utilization target for first-wave = 0.6 (we keep headroom for spikes). GPUs_needed_raw = ceil(10000 / (6300 * 0.6)) = ceil(10000 / 3780) = 3 GPUs. Add 20% spare -> 4 GPUs.
- Recommendation: prefer 4x A100-80GB (or 8x H100-encap depending on availability) in 1 rack for minimal-latency, single-region private cluster.

Latency-backed BOM heuristics (short checklist):
- If p95 latency budget < 120ms, steer to higher-memory GPUs (80GB+) or sharded multi-GPU inference patterns.
- If workload has long-context (>2k tokens), use additional KV memory per request; reduce effective throughput by 30% for capacity calc.
- If KV cache hit rate > 50%, effective tokens/sec demand can be reduced equivalently; re-run calc with reduced baseline.
- For early onramp, prefer odd-numbered GPU counts (3/5/7) only if autoscaling/eviction is well-tested; otherwise use power-of-two or multiples of chassis slots for simpler ops.

First-wave BOM (example lines with quick-cost heuristics):
CSV_TABLE:
"Item,Qty,SKU/Spec,UnitNotes,LeadTimeWeeks,UnitCostUSD,MonthlyAmortizedUSD"
"Compute nodes,2,1U dual-socket chassis (4x GPU slots) - 2 nodes per rack typical, empty for now,2-4,8000,220"
"GPUs,4,NVIDIA A100 80GB (alternative: H100 80GB if available),6-12,40000,1200"
"NVMe cache (per-node),4,4TB NVMe (PCIe4) for KV/caching,2-3,700,20"
"Switching,1,Top-of-rack 100Gbps switch (40x 100G ports recommended),2-4,6000,160"
"PSU + PDUs,1,Redundant PSUs per chassis + monitored PDU,2-3,1500,40"
"Rack + rails + kitting,1,Standard 42U rack + caging + racking service,1-2,1200,35"
"Network uplinks,2,2x 100G optics for uplink/peering,1-2,1500,45"
"KMS/HSM appliance,0 or 1,Optional if required by customer (cloud KMS can be used),4-8,8000,220"
"Spare GPU pool,1 (spare),Mobile spare or hot-swap policy recommended,variable,40000,1200"

Notes on the CSV table: UnitCostUSD are order-of-magnitude; monthly amortized assumes 36-month straight-line for compute and 60-month for rack/network as approximate. Adjust based on procurement terms.

Operational policies and recommended defaults for first-wave:
- Autoscaling: set conservative min replicas to 1 per chassis and max to cover 2x expected baseline tokens/sec. Use scheduled scaling for expected daily peaks.
- Patch/maintenance windows: weekly small-window patching; monthly deeper kernel/firmware updates. Maintain 1 hot-swap spare GPU in the lab for first 3 months.
- Monitoring: emit token-level counters, KV-cache hit/miss, per-GPU utilization, and p95/p99 latency per route. Configure alerts at 70% continuous GPU utilization and p95 crossing SLA.
- Rollout checklist (high level):
  * Week 0-2: confirmation of SKU availability + finalize network peering and IP ranges with customer.
  * Week 3-6: procurement + rack scheduling.
  * Week 6-8: on-site racking & network install (if on-prem) or VPC peering & test jobs (if coloc).
  * Week 8-10: smoke tests, canary traffic at 10% of baseline, HA tests (power/network failover).

Edge cases and common gotchas:
- If customer demands multi-region active-active, duplicate the BOM x regions + 15% inter-region spare for failover; network egress costs often dominate.
- Oversubscribing with lower memory cards (e.g., 48GB) can appear cheaper but will force model swaps and increase latency variability — document this tradeoff in proposals.
- Cooling and power: check site power per rack (kW) early; GPUs like H100/A100 at full load can approach 6–8kW per rack at high density.

Appendix A — Short model of quick-calculator pseudocode:
- INPUTS: concurrent_sessions, tokens_per_session, think_time_s, model_throughput_per_gpu, bench_safety_factor, utilization_target, spare_pct
- baseline_tps = (concurrent_sessions * tokens_per_session) / think_time_s
- per_gpu_effective = model_throughput_per_gpu * bench_safety_factor
- raw_gpus = ceil(baseline_tps / (per_gpu_effective * utilization_target))
- recommended_gpus = ceil(raw_gpus * (1 + spare_pct))

Appendix B — Suggested follow-ups (action items):
- Sales-Eng: confirm expected traffic shape + request 72-hour sample trace if available.
- Solutions: pick model parity option (latency-focused vs cost-focused) and produce 2 BOM variants.
- Procurement: validate preferred vendor lead times and alternative SKUs.
- Infra Ops: validate power + network port counts at customer site and confirm cage dimensions.

Revision history:
- 2026-01-10: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2026-01-18: added conservative benching multiplier and sample CSV (Omar)
- 2026-02-03: clarified rack density notes and timeline (Priya)

Scratchpad / quick questions to resolve in scoping call:
- Do they require on-prem KMS/HSM or is cloud KMS acceptable?
- Are there regulatory constraints on spare GPUs/devices being offsite?
- Preferred vendor for rack installation (vendor options and OLA SLA)?

End of document.
